challenge.better_approach: Reading the script file a command runs and applying the co-occurrence to its text was looked at; scripts build record paths by glob and variables, so text cannot see what they will write. Measuring the working copy after the command sees every shape.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a record dirty in the working copy whose bytes match no journal entry was written by the command just run; one written earlier and left unparked fires on every call until parked or reverted, which is the intended nag.
challenge.prior_art: cairn artifact check (check_staged) already compares staged bytes against the journal at commit; this asks the same question of the working copy, through the same door's last_sha and locate, rebuilding neither.
challenge.real_collision: None with artifactgate's co-occurrence trade: PreToolUse still refuses the shapes it sees; this is the after-the-fact measure for the shapes it cannot.

answers.falsifier: Done when a Bash command running a script file that writes a scratch ticket passes PreToolUse and is named by PostToolUse, a door write and a dirty non-record are not named, and the hook is registered. Wrong intent if the PostToolUse pass costs more than ~200 ms a Bash call on the house trees, or names records CC did not touch.
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured on ticket b7068b1ba431 in bin/cmd/artifactgate (verdict reads only the command text)
answers.how: bin/cmd/artifactgate gains a PostToolUse branch for Bash: it lists each root's working-copy changed record paths (git status, filtered by the door's locate) whose bytes do not hash to the journal's last entry for that path, and exits 2 naming each with the way through (cairn artifact hand-edit). .claude/settings.json registers it under PostToolUse. The PreToolUse co-occurrence stays as the cheap first refusal.
answers.traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy): the journal's who/when record is the rule; today a script-file write meets it only at commit, after the edit is made. Also Law 7: the miss is loud at the diagnostic surface the moment it happens.
answers.what: A Bash command that writes a record of truth around the artifact door is named to CC right after it runs, whatever shape the write took, instead of first at commit.

bullets.text: Measured 2026-11-18: artifactgate's verdict() returns allow (exit 0) for `python3 <scratch>/w.py` whose body writes a ticket; only the commit check catches it.
